title: Gustar: saying what you like
summary: Me gusta el café, me gustan los gatos, me gusta bailar: the verb that works backwards.
focus: Gustar and similar verbs (encantar, doler) with indirect object pronouns
content:
## Gustar works backwards

*Gustar* literally means *to be pleasing*. The thing you like is the **subject**, and you are the person it pleases:

- *Me gusta el café.* I like coffee (coffee is pleasing to me).
- *Me gustan los gatos.* I like cats (cats are pleasing to me).

So the verb agrees with the **thing**: singular **gusta**, plural **gustan**.

## The person: me, te, le…

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| me gusta | I like | *Me gusta la música.* |
| te gusta | you like | *¿Te gusta el fútbol?* |
| le gusta | he / she / you (formal) like | *Le gusta leer.* |
| nos gusta | we like | *Nos gusta la playa.* |
| os gusta | you all like | *¿Os gusta España?* |
| les gusta | they / you all like | *Les gustan los perros.* |

The thing liked usually takes an article: *me gusta **el** chocolate*, not *me gusta chocolate*.

## Liking an activity

With a verb, use the infinitive and singular *gusta*: *Me gusta bailar.* *Nos gusta viajar y comer bien.*

## Making the person clear, or emphatic

*Le gusta* could be he, she or you. Add **a + person**: *A Marta le gusta el cine. A usted le gusta el té.* For emphasis or contrast: *A mí me gusta, pero a ti no.*

## Friends of gustar

- **encantar** (to love): *Me encanta el chocolate. Me encantan las fiestas.*
- **doler** (to hurt): *Me duele la cabeza. Me duelen los pies.*
- **interesar**, **importar**, **molestar** work the same way.

Negative: *No me gusta el frío.* Agreeing: *A mí también / A mí tampoco.*

quiz.explanation: El café is singular, so gusta.
Los gatos is plural, so gustan.
The person is nos; la playa is singular, so gusta.
An activity goes in the infinitive: te gusta bailar.

quiz.prompt: Complete: A Marta ___ gusta el cine.

quiz.explanation: Doler works like gustar; la cabeza is singular: duele.

quiz.prompt: — No me gusta el frío. — A mí ___.
quiz.explanation: Agreeing with a negative: a mí tampoco.
Encantar agrees with las fiestas (plural), so encantan, and the people are les.

listening.note: The thing liked keeps its article.
Gustan agrees with the plural thing.
New word: el pie = the foot.

listening.text: A Luis no le gusta bailar.
listening.note: An activity takes the infinitive and singular gusta.

listening.text: Me gusta mucho el helado de chocolate.
listening.meaning: I really like chocolate ice cream.
listening.note: New word: el helado = the ice cream.

listening.text: Me gusta leer, pero no me gusta estudiar.
listening.meaning: I like reading, but I don't like studying.

listening.text: A Ana le gusta la música, pero a mí me gusta más el fútbol.
listening.meaning: Ana likes music, but I like football more.

conversations.title: Likes and dislikes
conversations.scenario: Two new friends compare their tastes.

lines.meaning: I love it. And I really like dancing.

lines.text: A mí también. ¿Te gustan los perros?
lines.meaning: Me too. Do you like dogs?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No, no me gustan. Me gustan los gatos.

lines.meaning: My sister loves cats. She has three.

lines.meaning: And what do you like doing on Sundays?

lines.text: Me gusta leer en la playa, pero hoy me duele la cabeza.
lines.meaning: I like reading on the beach, but today my head hurts.

lines.text: Entonces nos quedamos en casa. ¿Te gusta el chocolate?
lines.meaning: Then we stay home. Do you like chocolate?

bites.title: The thing is the subject
bites.rule: Gustar works backwards: the thing you like is the subject, so the verb agrees with IT, not with you. One thing: gusta. Several things: gustan.
bites.example: Me gusta el café. Me gustan los gatos.
bites.example_meaning: I like coffee. I like cats.

bites.title: Never 'yo gusto'
bites.rule: The person who likes goes in front as a little pronoun: me, te, le, nos, os, les. Then gusta or gustan.

bites.title: Activities count as one
bites.rule: Liking doing something? Use the infinitive and keep gusta singular, even with two activities.
bites.example: Nos gusta viajar y comer bien.
bites.example_meaning: We like travelling and eating well.

bites.title: A + person clears it up
bites.rule: Le gusta could be he, she or you, so add a + person: a Marta le gusta. Encantar (to love) and doler (to hurt) work exactly the same way.
bites.example: A Marta le encanta el chocolate.

sorts.title: Gusta or gustan?
sorts.why: Gusta for one thing or any activity (infinitive); gustan for plural things.

sorts.title: Which pronoun?

items.text: A mis padres ___ gustan los perros.

sorts.why: The pronoun names who is pleased: me (I), te (you), le (he, she, usted), les (they, ustedes).

spots.why: Marta is 'she', so the pronoun is le.
An activity after gustar goes in the infinitive.
